cues.en: Leaving Earth to find new homes in space is an old dream of humanity and will sooner or later be necessary for our survival.
cues.zh: 离开地球，在太空中寻找新家园，是人类长久以来的梦想，而且迟早会成为我们生存的必需。

cues.en: The planet that gets the most attention is Mars, a small, toxic,
cues.zh: 最受关注的行星是火星，一颗微小、有毒、

cues.en: and energy poor planet that just about seems good enough for a colony of depressed humans huddled in underground cities.
cues.zh: 且能源匮乏的行星，似乎勉强够一群抑郁的人类蜷缩在地下城市里建立殖民地。

cues.en: But what if we think bigger?
cues.zh: 但如果我们把眼光放得更大呢？

cues.en: What if we take Venus, one of the most hostile and deadly places in the solar system, and turn it into a colony?
cues.zh: 如果我们把金星——太阳系中最恶劣、最致命的地方之一——变成殖民地呢？

cues.en: Not by building lofty cloud cities, but by creating a proper second Earth.
cues.zh: 不是建造高耸的云中城市，而是打造一个真正的第二地球。

cues.en: It might be easier than you think.
cues.zh: 这可能比你想象的更容易。

cues.en: Venus is by far the hottest planet in the solar system with a surface temperature of 460
cues.zh: 金星是太阳系中迄今为止最热的行星，表面温度达460

cues.en: degrees Celsius, hot enough to melt lead.
cues.zh: 摄氏度，热到足以熔化铅。

cues.en: This heat is due to the most extreme greenhouse effect in the solar system.
cues.zh: 这种高温源于太阳系中最极端的温室效应。

cues.en: CO two is great at trapping heat. Even a rise from 0.03%
cues.zh: 二氧化碳极擅长锁住热量。甚至从0.03%

cues.en: in Earth's atmosphere is heating up our planet right now.
cues.zh: 的地球大气变化，此刻就在让我们的星球升温。

cues.en: Venus's atmosphere is 97%
cues.zh: 金星的大气中97%

cues.en: c o two.
cues.zh: 是二氧化碳。

cues.en: Also, Venus's atmosphere is 93 times denser than Earth's.
cues.zh: 此外，金星大气的密度是地球的93倍。

cues.en: Standing on Venus's surface would feel like taking a dive about 900 meters deep into the ocean. The pressure would kill you instantly.
cues.zh: 站在金星表面，感觉就像潜入约900米深的海洋。压力会瞬间要了你的命。

cues.en: It's a truly horrible place, so why should we even bother?
cues.zh: 这真是个可怕的地方，那我们何必费心呢？

cues.en: First and foremost, Venus is almost as big as Earth and has 90% of its surface gravity.
cues.zh: 首先也是最重要的，金星几乎和地球一样大，表面重力是地球的90%。

cues.en: Surface gravity is a big problem when colonizing the solar system because it's very likely that long stays in low gravity places will have negative health effects.
cues.zh: 在殖民太阳系时，表面重力是个大问题，因为长期待在低重力环境很可能对健康产生负面影响。

cues.en: Venus' size means it could be the second largest habitat in the solar system. A new home for billions of humans and trillions of animals with oceans,
cues.zh: 从金星的体积来看，它完全可以成为太阳系第二大宜居地。成为数十亿人类和数万亿动物的新家园，拥有海洋、

cues.en: lush forests, and a beautiful blue sky.
cues.zh: 茂密的森林和美丽蔚蓝的天空。

cues.en: A properly terraformed Venus may be the most pleasant place to live outside of Earth.
cues.zh: 经过充分地球化改造的金星，可能是地球之外最舒适的宜居之地。

cues.en: While we can't exactly terraform Venus today, a slightly more ambitious future version of us could take this project on.
cues.zh: 尽管我们现在还无法改造金星，但未来更有雄心的人类完全可以承担这项工程。

cues.en: It will take a few generations to complete and be a huge challenge like building the Great Pyramids was for our ancestors.
cues.zh: 这需要耗费数代人才能完成，就像祖先建造大金字塔一样，是一项巨大的挑战。

cues.en: But then, it's not like humans have never started projects that took more than a lifetime to complete.
cues.zh: 但话又说回来，人类又不是没启动过跨越一生的世纪工程。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好吧。

cues.en: Let's do it.
cues.zh: 开始动手吧。

cues.en: Before anything else, we need to cool Venus down and remove the gas that makes up the extremely heavy atmosphere.
cues.zh: 首先，我们需要给金星降温，并清除构成其极其厚重大气层的气体。

cues.en: As mentioned, there's a lot of it. Around 465,000,000
cues.zh: 正如之前提到的，这些气体的量极为庞大。大约有 465,000,000

cues.en: tons.
cues.zh: 吨。

cues.en: How do we do that? There are a few options. We could create giant solar collectors powering a huge array of laser beams that heat up the atmosphere so much that it's blasted into space.
cues.zh: 该怎么做？有几个方案。我们可以建造巨大的太阳能集热器，为庞大的激光阵列供电，将大气层加热到足以被轰入太空。

cues.en: Although we would need thousands of times the entire power generating capacity of humanity, and it would still take thousands of years to remove the atmosphere.
cues.zh: 不过这需要全人类发电总量的数千倍，而且仍要花上数千年才能清除这层大气。

cues.en: Another way is to sequester the atmosphere,
cues.zh: 另一种方法是封存这层大气，

cues.en: binding the c o two in different compounds through chemical reactions.
cues.zh: 通过化学反应将二氧化碳结合成不同的化合物。

cues.en: We could mine elements like calcium or magnesium on mercury and shoot them at Venus via mass driver systems,
cues.zh: 我们可以在水星上开采钙或镁等元素，再用质量投射系统将它们射向金星，

cues.en: electric rails that make rockets unnecessary
cues.zh: 这种电磁轨道能彻底摆脱对火箭的依赖，

cues.en: on smaller planets.
cues.zh: 尤其是在较小的行星上。

cues.en: The metals would combine to bind the c o two into different carbonates
cues.zh: 这些金属会结合，把二氧化碳固定成不同的碳酸盐

cues.en: basically forever,
cues.zh: 基本上永久地，

cues.en: but the scale makes the whole thing impractical.
cues.zh: 但规模让整件事变得不切实际。

cues.en: We would need several 100,000,000,000
cues.zh: 我们需要几千亿吨

cues.en: tons of material to sequester the c o two this way.
cues.zh: 的材料才能以这种方式封存二氧化碳。

cues.en: Seems like a waste of material that might take too long.
cues.zh: 看起来像是浪费材料，而且可能耗时太久。

cues.en: An equally ridiculous idea that could actually work is to put Venus in the shade,
cues.zh: 一个同样荒谬但确实可能奏效的想法是，给金星遮阳，

cues.en: literally,
cues.zh: 字面意义上的，

cues.en: by constructing a huge mirror to blot out the sun to just freeze the atmosphere.
cues.zh: 通过建造一面巨大的镜子来遮挡太阳，仅仅为了冻结大气层。

cues.en: The mirror doesn't need to be complex or massive, just a very thin foil with a little structural support.
cues.zh: 这面镜子不需要复杂或庞大，只需要一层非常薄的箔片，加上一点结构支撑。

cues.en: Building such a large flat surface so close to the sun will turn it effectively into a solar sail and push it out of position. So instead of one giant circular object, our mirror will consist of many different pieces.
cues.zh: 在如此靠近太阳的地方建造这么大的平面，会使其实际上变成太阳帆，把它推离原位。所以我们的镜子不是一整块巨大的圆形物体，而是由许多不同的部件组成。

cues.en: Annular slacks of angled mirrors can reflect sunlight from one set of mirrors to the next. Mirrors would be angled, reflecting light from one to another until the light is redirected to the back, balancing the force on the front and holding them in position.
cues.zh: 倾斜镜面的环形松弛阵列可以把阳光从一组镜子反射到下一组。镜子会倾斜，将光从一面反射到另一面，直到光被重新导向后方，平衡前面的受力，让它们保持在位。

cues.en: After a few years of getting the infrastructure in place, things start slowly and then escalate.
cues.zh: 在几年内把基础设施建好后，事情开始缓慢推进，然后逐步升级。

cues.en: For the first few decades, the atmosphere slowly cools down, but stays dense and deadly.
cues.zh: 最初几十年里，大气缓慢冷却，但仍然浓密而致命。

cues.en: Until after some sixty years, it reaches the critical temperature of 31 degrees Celsius.
cues.zh: 直到大约六十年后，它达到31摄氏度的临界温度。

cues.en: Suddenly, the great flood begins on Venus as c o two turns to liquid at this pressure and begins to rain down.
cues.zh: 突然间，金星上爆发了大洪水，二氧化碳在这个压力下变成液体，开始倾盆而下。

cues.en: A constant global rainstorm of unbelievable proportions lasting thirty years.
cues.zh: 一场规模惊人、持续三十年的全球性暴雨。

cues.en: The pressure and temperature suddenly begin to drop in unison.
cues.zh: 压力和温度突然开始同步下降。

cues.en: For almost a century, puddles turn into lakes and oceans.
cues.zh: 在将近一个世纪的时间里，水洼变成了湖泊和海洋。

cues.en: The surface temperature is now minus 56 degrees Celsius, and the pressure has dropped to only seven times the pressure on Earth.
cues.zh: 地表温度现在为零下56摄氏度，压力也降到了只有地球表面压力的七倍。

cues.en: Finally, at a really unpleasant minus 81 degrees Celsius, the c o two oceans begin to freeze and the rain turns into snow.
cues.zh: 最后，在令人极不适的零下81摄氏度，二氧化碳海洋开始冻结，降雨变成了降雪。

cues.en: This leaves us with a frozen Venus covered in oceans as hard as rock and gigantic c o two glaciers.
cues.zh: 这就给我们留下了一个冰冻的金星，表面覆盖着坚如岩石的海洋和巨大的二氧化碳冰川。

cues.en: What remains of the atmosphere is mostly nitrogen at about three times Earth's surface pressure.
cues.zh: 剩下的大气主要是氮气，约为地球表面压力的三倍。

cues.en: If you don't mind freezing and suffocating, you can now take a stroll over Venus's surface.
cues.zh: 如果你不介意被冻死和窒息，现在就可以在金星表面散步了。

cues.en: But the frozen c o two remains a bit of a problem. At some point, want we to warm up the planet, but if we do, the c o two ice will melt and fill up the atmosphere again. So we need some way to keep it from doing that.
cues.zh: 但冻结的二氧化碳仍然是个问题。某个时候我们想给这颗行星升温，但一旦升温，二氧化碳冰就会融化，再次充满大气层。所以我们需要某种方法阻止这种情况发生。

cues.en: One is to simply cover it all with cheap plastic insulation and cover it up with ground up Venus rock water oceans.
cues.zh: 一种方法是用廉价塑料隔热层把它全部盖住，再铺上碾碎的金星岩石和水海洋。

cues.en: Although some planetary scientists will be very stressed out about us building a new planet containing a potential time bomb like that.
cues.zh: 不过，有些行星科学家会对我们建造一个包含这种潜在定时炸弹的新行星感到非常焦虑。

cues.en: A few unfortunately timed volcanoes could melt a lot of c o two at once and ruin everything.
cues.zh: 几个时机不巧的火山可能一次性融化大量二氧化碳，毁掉一切。

cues.en: Another obvious solution is to shoot it all out into space and collect it into a small moon for storage and future use. We can make this more efficient by using mass drivers instead of rockets, but moving all that mass will still be a pretty intense challenge that will take some time to solve.
cues.zh: 另一个显而易见的方案是把它们全部射入太空，聚集成为一个小卫星储存起来，供未来使用。我们可以用质量驱动器代替火箭来提高效率，但移动这么多质量仍然是一个相当艰巨的挑战，需要一些时间来解决。

cues.en: Whatever we end up doing with the atmosphere, to move forward, we need water, which we could get from ice moons.
cues.zh: 无论我们最终如何处理大气，要继续推进，我们需要水，而水可以从冰卫星上获取。

cues.en: Europa, a moon of Jupiter, has twice as much water as Earth's oceans.
cues.zh: 木星的卫星木卫二拥有的水量是地球海洋的两倍。

cues.en: Now, catching a moon and transporting it through the solar system is not exactly easy.
cues.zh: 不过，捕获一颗卫星并把它运送穿越太阳系可不太容易。

cues.en: So instead, it might be easier to cut chunks of ice off Europa with an army of construction drones and shoot them at Venus using more of those mass drivers.
cues.zh: 所以，更简单的做法可能是用一群建筑无人机从木卫二上切下冰块，再用更多质量驱动器把它们射向金星。

cues.en: Space tethers could save us a lot of effort and energy here. We made a whole video explaining how they work, but in a nutshell, they are slings that can take a payload on both ends.
cues.zh: 太空缆索可以在这里帮我们省下大量精力和能量。我们做过一整期视频讲解它们的工作原理，但简而言之，它们就是两端都能承载载荷的投石索。

cues.en: On Europa, they do most of the work needed to catapult our ice to Venus.
cues.zh: 在木卫二上，它们完成了把我们的冰弹射到金星所需的大部分工作。

cues.en: The ice hits the Venus tethers, which gently drop it into the atmosphere where it falls down as snow.
cues.zh: 冰块击中金星的缆索，缆索将其轻轻送入大气层，冰在那里以雪的形式落下。

cues.en: In exchange, the Venus tethers get to catch c o two ice shot up from below and accelerated
cues.zh: 作为交换，金星的缆索可以接住从下方射上来并加速

cues.en: into orbit.
cues.zh: 进入轨道的二氧化碳冰。

cues.en: We can remove excess nitrogen using this same method to further lower our atmospheric pressure.
cues.zh: 我们可以用同样的方法去除多余的氮气，进一步降低大气压。

cues.en: After a few decades or centuries, Venus would be covered by a nice shallow frozen ocean a few 100 meters deep.
cues.zh: 几十年或数百年后，金星表面会覆盖一层数百米深的浅薄冰洋。

cues.en: It would look extremely different from today.
cues.zh: 它看起来将与今天截然不同。

cues.en: A few continents and countless islands have formed.
cues.zh: 几块大陆和无数岛屿已经形成。

cues.en: This is beginning to look a bit like our planet.
cues.zh: 这开始有点像我们的地球了。

cues.en: Now the last and most magnificent phase of terraforming begins, making the atmosphere breathable and adding life.
cues.zh: 现在进入地球化改造最后、也是最宏伟的阶段：让大气变得适宜呼吸，并引入生命。

cues.en: First, we need light though, and we need to heat the planet up again.
cues.zh: 不过我们首先需要光照，得让这颗星球重新升温。

cues.en: A Venus day is two thousand eight hundred and two hours long, more than one hundred and sixteen Earth days.
cues.zh: 金星的一天长达 2802 个小时，相当于 116 个地球日以上。

cues.en: So if we just remove our giant mirror, we would grill half of our planet.
cues.zh: 所以如果直接撤掉巨型反射镜，就会把半个星球烤焦。

cues.en: Even without the massive atmosphere, temperatures would reach unbearable
cues.zh: 即使没有浓厚的大气层，温度也会达到难以忍受的

cues.en: levels.
cues.zh: 地步。

cues.en: The simplest way to create a day night cycle and let some energy in again is with another set of mirrors to illuminate our continents and melt our water oceans,
cues.zh: 建立昼夜循环并重新引入能量最简单的办法，是用另一套反射镜来照亮大陆并融化冰洋，

cues.en: which would let us completely control how much energy we get and where it goes.
cues.zh: 这样我们就能完全掌控获取多少能量以及能量输送到哪里。

cues.en: The atmosphere is now mostly made up of nitrogen and basically devoid of oxygen.
cues.zh: 此时的大气主要由氮气构成，几乎完全没有氧气。

cues.en: So the first inhabitants will likely be trillions and trillions of cyanobacteria,
cues.zh: 因此第一批居民很可能是数以万亿计的蓝细菌，

cues.en: which can get photosynthesizing
cues.zh: 它们可以进行光合作用

cues.en: and release oxygen.
cues.zh: 并释放氧气。

cues.en: We know that they can quickly turn around the atmosphere of a planet because billions of years ago, they were probably responsible for turning the toxic atmosphere of our young earth into an atmosphere with enough oxygen for more complex animal life.
cues.zh: 我们知道它们能迅速改变行星的大气环境，因为数十亿年前，很可能正是它们把幼年地球的有毒大气，改造成了氧气充足、足以孕育更复杂动物生命的环境。

cues.en: But not only that. Cyanobacteria
cues.zh: 不仅如此，蓝细菌

cues.en: can fix nitrogen from the atmosphere and turn it into nutrients that can be used by living beings.
cues.zh: 能够固定大气中的氮，将其转化为生物可利用的养分。

cues.en: This way, they will essentially fertilize our dead ocean water and prepare it for more complex organisms.
cues.zh: 这样一来，它们就能实质上滋养这片死寂的海洋，为更复杂的生命铺平道路。

cues.en: On land, our colonists need to grind down some of the former Venusian surface to make soil for nitrogen
cues.zh: 在陆地上，殖民者需要磨碎部分原金星地表制成土壤，供固氮……

cues.en: fixing plants to grow on.
cues.zh: ……植物生长。

cues.en: Eventually, billions of trees would spread, creating large forests covering massive parts of the continents.
cues.zh: 最终，数十亿棵树木繁衍开来，形成覆盖大片陆地的广袤森林。

cues.en: Venus would turn green.
cues.zh: 金星将染上一片翠绿。

cues.en: To speed things up, c o two would be strategically released to supply the plants and cyanobacteria.
cues.zh: 为了加速这一过程，还可以有策略地释放二氧化碳，供给植物和蓝细菌。

cues.en: Areas already covered with plants could get extra daylight from our orbital mirrors, so the plants would be active for most of each day.
cues.zh: 已经长出植物的区域还能通过轨道镜获得额外光照，使植物在一天中的大部分时间里都保持活跃。

cues.en: Maybe we won't have to do this with the same plants and animals we know today.
cues.zh: 也许我们根本不必局限于今天所熟知的动植物。

cues.en: As genetic engineering matures and our understanding of genetics and the machinery of life expands,
cues.zh: 随着基因工程日益成熟，以及对遗传学和生命机制理解的加深，

cues.en: we might just engineer life as we need it. All in all, it would take several thousand years to make the atmosphere breathable by humans.
cues.zh: 我们完全可以按需定制生命。总的来说，要让大气达到人类可直接呼吸的程度，需要耗费数千年。

cues.en: In the meantime, you could stroll around with nothing more than regular clothes and an oxygen mask.
cues.zh: 在此期间，你只需穿普通衣服、戴上氧气面罩，就能在户外漫步。

cues.en: Settlers would enjoy a vast new planet filled with resources and bathed in sunlight.
cues.zh: 定居者将拥有一颗沐浴在阳光下、资源丰饶的辽阔新星球。

cues.en: They might think of new ways to use the vast amounts of carbon
cues.zh: 他们或许会想出新办法，来利用上空轨道中大量的碳、

cues.en: ice and nitrogen orbiting in space above,
cues.zh: 冰和氮，

cues.en: industrial processes, rocket fuel, or even boosting the terraforming of another planet like tiny Mars.
cues.zh: 将其用于工业生产、火箭燃料，甚至加速推进像小巧的火星这样另一颗行星的地球化。

cues.en: Venus is fully terraformed.
cues.zh: Venus已经完全地球化了。

cues.en: Animals roam through vast ecosystems.
cues.zh: 动物们在广阔生态系统中自由活动。

cues.en: Cities are being constructed.
cues.zh: 城市正在建设中。

cues.en: Billions of settlers and their descendants make this world their home.
cues.zh: 数十亿定居者及其后代把这里当成了家。

cues.en: They will see images of the past, how Venus was once the most hostile planet around,
cues.zh: 他们会看到过去的影像，看到金星曾经是周围最不宜居的行星，

cues.en: how it took hundreds of years to freeze hell and to ship in the oceans, and another few thousand years to make it possible to breathe freely.
cues.zh: 看到花了数百年才冻结地狱般的环境、运来海洋，又花了几千年才让自由呼吸成为可能。

cues.en: They will barely be able to believe it.
cues.zh: 他们几乎不敢相信。

cues.en: Okay. Maybe it's not that easy to terra form Venus, and a lot of things must go right for this future to become reality.
cues.zh: 好吧，也许改造金星没那么容易，要让这个未来成真，很多环节都必须顺利。

cues.en: But it is possible, and with technology that is within the reach of a motivated and slightly more advanced humanity that wants to venture into space.
cues.zh: 但这是可能的，而且所用的技术，是一个有动力、稍微更先进、渴望探索太空的人类所能掌握的。

cues.en: The only thing that's stopping it is our imagination,
cues.zh: 唯一阻碍我们的，是我们的想象力，

cues.en: and that, at least, is a problem that's easy to overcome.
cues.zh: 而至少这个问题，很容易克服。

cues.en: Welcome to the Kurzgesagt
cues.zh: 欢迎来到Kurzgesagt

cues.en: lab. Let's conduct a few stellar experiments.
cues.zh: 实验室。我们来做几个恒星实验。

cues.en: We'll first add some more mass to this protostar.
cues.zh: 先给这颗原恒星增加一些质量。

cues.en: More.
cues.zh: 再多点。

cues.en: A bit more.
cues.zh: 再多一点。

cues.en: Wow. We've just created a blue giant, a stunger with 10 times the mass of our sun. Let's now add a couple of million years and see what happens.
cues.zh: 哇。我们刚创造了一颗蓝巨星，质量是太阳的10倍。现在快进几百万年，看看会发生什么。

cues.en: A supernova,
cues.zh: 一场超新星爆发，

cues.en: breathtaking.
cues.zh: 令人惊叹。

cues.en: And look, it leaves behind a black hole.
cues.zh: 看，它留下了一个黑洞。

cues.en: Fascinating stuff.
cues.zh: 真是奇妙。

cues.en: Now we record our findings.
cues.zh: 现在记录我们的发现。

cues.en: Be careful to preserve the sparkle.
cues.zh: 小心保留那份闪光。

cues.en: It's now time for Duck's final inspection.
cues.zh: 现在到了Duck的最终检查时间。

cues.en: This one is always a nail biter. He has incredibly high standards.
cues.zh: 这一项总是让人紧张。他的标准高得离谱。

cues.en: Lucky for us, our work is scientifically accurate, offers an overview of important
cues.zh: 幸运的是，我们的作品不仅科学严谨，概述了重要的

cues.en: astrophysical processes,
cues.zh: 天体物理过程，

cues.en: and is a real stunner.
cues.zh: 而且视觉效果相当惊艳。

cues.en: Duck approves.
cues.zh: 小鸭子表示认可。

cues.en: Looks like it's ready to be shared with the world as a poster, a very special piece of Kurzgesagt you can take home and touch.
cues.zh: 看来它可以做成海报与大家见面了，这是一件你可以带回家亲手触摸的、非常特别的 Kurzgesagt 周边。

cues.en: You can get this very special poster along with many other science y and space y things created with love and care from our shop.
cues.zh: 你可以在我们的网店里买到这张特别的海报，以及许多用心制作、充满科学与太空趣味的好物。

cues.en: Every Kurzgesagt product you buy directly funds another moment we get to spend working on our videos.
cues.zh: 你购买的每一件 Kurzgesagt 产品，都会直接资助我们投入更多时间制作视频。

cues.en: Thank you so much for being a part of our story and for making this channel possible.
cues.zh: 非常感谢你成为我们故事的一部分，让这个频道得以延续。
